hero.subtitle: When a defective product injures someone in Norco, California law often doesn't require proving the maker was careless—just that the product was flawed and caused harm. We can review your claim at no cost and explain your options under California law.

about.title: Norco Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Norco's mix of equestrian trails, ranch properties, and busy corridors like Hamner Avenue and 6th Street means residents rely daily on everything from vehicle parts and farm equipment to household appliances and safety gear. When one of those products fails because of a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or a missing warning, the resulting injury can be serious and sudden. California generally applies strict liability in these cases, meaning the person hurt doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was negligent—only that the product itself was defective and that the defect caused the harm. Liability can extend beyond the manufacturer to distributors and retailers who placed the product into the stream of commerce. If you were hurt by a product in Norco, holding onto the item and any packaging can matter. We handle product liability claims and can review what happened to explain the options available under California law.
commonInjuries: Burns from malfunctioning appliances or equipment
Traumatic injuries from failed vehicle or auto parts
Crush or amputation injuries from farm or ranch machinery
Chemical exposure from mislabeled or unsafe products
Fractures from collapsing furniture or structural products
Injuries from defective safety or protective gear

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, we may be able to focus on proving the defect and the harm rather than the manufacturer's state of mind.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may broaden where compensation could come from.

items.title: Guidance on Preserving Evidence
items.desc: Our team can advise you early on keeping the product, packaging, and receipts intact, since physical evidence often matters most in these claims.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability law often works on a strict liability basis, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and caused your injury, not that someone was negligent. We can review the specifics of your situation to explain how this applies.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep the product, any packaging, instructions, and your receipt exactly as they were after the incident. This evidence can be important whether the defect involved a vehicle part, an appliance, or farm equipment common in a community like Norco. Avoid repairing or discarding it before speaking with us.

items.question: Can I still pursue a claim if the injury happened outside of Norco but I live here?
items.answer: Yes, where you live doesn't limit whether you can pursue a claim under California law. What matters more is where the product was purchased, used, or where the injury occurred. We can still review your case regardless of where the incident took place.
